KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.1.Title: Sand-worn Leather Tome
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.1.Text:
We had honour once, long, long ago. On a world of emerald leaves, we hunted our prey without blade nor bow, and took only what we needed. This Lougrim taught us, may her memory never fade.

The abomination slew Lougrim, not for honour, not for the hunt, but for the love of power. She enslaved our people, turned us into footsoldiers for wars we should never have been a part of. Took our young and trained them to be killers, murderers, not the hunters we should be. Honour stripped out in favour of bloodlust, and too many of our kin agreed.

So, what could we do but leave?

We passed through forests, mountains and lost many along the way. Those of us who chose to follow the guidance of the moon, rather than the dragon queen’s willow-wisp firelight. We shall preserve the honour of our people, well, what little is left.

I am old now, the ache in my bones tells me that my time comes to an end. This great desert before me shall be my tomb, yet, I will die free. I will die as a true garou, a hunter, not a killer. When my body rests beneath the sands, let it begin a healing cycle for my people. Let this land flourish, and my people with it.

Let us be the children of the moon again.
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.2.Title: Sun-scorched Recipe Book
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.2.Text:
Snake, I’ve always wanted to try snake. My grandmother told me once of a stew that used it, how the venom gave a spicy little kick when you chowed down on the meat. Yet, I cannot find a single snake in the desert, no matter how hard I try.

I know they’re here. I’ve seen their tracks. I’ve discovered the remains of their kills. I’ve even seen the bite marks on the ankles of foolish garou who slept out in the sands. They’re real, they’re just hiding away from us, as if scared of something.

There is this old legend about snakes. I heard it from my father, who heard it from his mother, who heard it from, well, you know how all of this goes. The story goes that the desert once teamed with snakes. You couldn’t move for fear of fangs in your sandals when you weren’t looking. Poison killed more of us then anything else. It was a dark time for the clan.

Then, she came. The moon goddess, who moved like river water. She danced and danced, and the snakes danced with her. With each undulation, the snakes dug themselves into the sand, their writhing movements burying them deep. When the dance was done, the snakes had vanished beneath the dunes, never to threaten the people again.

It’s a nice story; I’ve always liked it.

Oh, but anyway, where was I? Ah yes, the recipe for the perfect cactus stew, all you need is…

[The rest of the page has been torn off]
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.3.Title: Chewed Doodle-Covered Journal
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.3.Text:
This journal is the property of Tazyn – age 9. DO NOT READ IT MUM!



I don’t know where mum is. I looked and I looked, but I couldn’t find her. I wandered only a little bit, just wanted to follow a pretty beetle I found, and now I don’t know where I am, or she is.

It’s scary out here. The wind keeps howling and there are things in the sand that wriggle and chase me. The vultures circle overheard as if waiting for me to fall.

Where’s mum? Why can’t she find me?





It got dark, then light again, and still no sign of mum. I slept under a big rock, it was cold and insects crawled all over me. I got spiders in my fur, I just know it.





I don’t know where I am. My mouth is so dry. I still can’t find mum. I’m so tired. Maybe if I sleep, all of this will go away and I’ll just wake up in my bed.





There was a voice, singing. Not like mum’s singing, this one was in tune. I followed it to a great river that wasn’t there yesterday and there was this woman just singing on a rock. She was the prettiest garou I ever saw. Eyes that sparkled like stars and silver fur like the moon. She wore this headdress that seemed to turn into water that dripped down into the river below.

She bade me drink, and it was delicious! Like fish soup and cactus juice, all rolled into one. I sat with her and she sang to me, banishing the shadows with her music. I fell asleep on her knees as she stroked my hair and promised I’d soon be home.

When I woke up, mum was fussing at me, brushing the sand from my fur. There was no river, nor silvery lady, but I was safe and found and could finally go home.

Thank you, weird singing moon lady! You’re the best.
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.4.Title: Gold-plated Tome
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.4.Text:
She came to us in our time of need and taught us the ways of the sand. A lost people, guided by her light into a new promised land for the garou. Not the forests of our homeworld, nor the roots of Ghornfell, but a world of dunes and  glittering nights, beneath the blazing sun.

She plucked a star from the sky and planted it in the sand, and where the silver light shone there sprouted crystal clear water that reflected the heavens above. She bade us drink from the waters and we were renewed, our past sins erased so that we could start afresh.

Stone, she taught us to twist and shape so that we could build houses, temples and monuments that would survive the sands long after we fell. Far sturdier than the wood and weave that we had relied on before. We tilled the dunes, finding the places where life could flourish and we planted seeds and crops at her directing, and from this desolate wasteland came life.

She was the moon and the river and the chance to start again. A mother to the garou when we needed guidance most.

To guide our way, she gave us the mirrors and the shards at the heart of them.  Silvered shards of moonlight, in physical form. They would act as beacons in the desert night, pointing the way to each of the settlements. A guiding light to banish the evils in our path.

Praise be to the moon.
Praise be El…

[The page has been damaged beyond repairing, obscuring the name]
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.5.Title: Ancient Text
KeysToEntries.FirstPeople.Book.5.Text:
This land, with all its strangeness, reminds me of the kingdom I once called home. The sand reminds me of the walks my husband and I shared together, our feet sinking into the grains as we discussed the wonders of the world.

The dunes, as they rise and fall, breathes into life the memories of our children, as they laughed and played with one another in the time before we granted them  immortality.

The brilliant, shining, sun, reminds me of him and how he lit up my world.

And the silence of the empty desert is a knife to my heart, reminding me that he is gone. I am  alone,  but the people here need not be.

They need someone to guide them, to lift them up and teach them the ways of the desert. Someone that can take their arboreal tendencies and reshape them into the wisdom of the dunes. I create oases, shielded by my protection, so that they might thrive in a world that would see them as dried up cadavers, forgotten and lost.

In me they see someone I am not. A goddess of the moon, like myself, but one who looked to the woods and not the waters I am more comfortable with. It is nice to be someone else for a while. To be needed, not because of some  aeon-long loyalty, but because I offer them a hope they thought was lost.

I will leave this world, soon, now that Guthix has laid his edicts. I will not return. Yet, I shall make sure that these people, my children of the moon, shall thrive in my absence.

It is nice to know that my legacy will be of something good. Something gained, rather than lost.
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.1.Title: Black-plated Tome
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.1.Text:
Darkness is the bane of all that is righteous. In the shadows does iniquity, criminality and cruelty thrive. Without illumination, all sins writhe in the umbral. Scorpions in the twilight, waiting to strike.

Yet fear not, oh blessed ones, because shadows burn in her great radiance. They retreat to the corners, cast out by her luminance, because she is the beacon that blinds the night.

She can place that light within you, oh faithful. She can let your soul shine like the star it was meant to be. You can be a glimmering mote of luminescence that reflects her divine corona, you can be a candle in the darkness, safe from the shadows.

Burn, oh faithful. Blaze and shine. Let the fire within you ignite the darkness, engulfing wickedness in her radiant flame.

She is the fire.

She is the light.

She is the ember of revelation in the kindling of our ignorance.

Praise be to her.

Praise be to her.

[The rest of the book has been torn apart, by great claw-like marks]
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.2.Title: Child’s Storybook
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.2.Text:
Once there was and once there wasn’t, long long ago, a cub called Aydahn, and he was always found where trouble brewed.

The baker he tricked with salt disguised as sugar. A hunter he tricked with animal noises stolen from the shaman’s magic bag. The elder he tricked with warnings of monsters, when none were around.

One night Aydahn found a cave in the desert, lit with flickering flames.

He called out to the cave, yet no reply did he get. Twice, then thrice, did he call to the cave, and on the third time it answered.

“Are you lost, little cub?” the cave called back to the boy. “I have sweets and secrets, if you just come inside.”

“Who lives in this cave?” Aydahn replied, tempted by treats but wise enough to doubt.

“I am the sun,” said the cavern, “resting for the night. Look to the sky and see my sister ride by. When she and her foxes race through the sky, I come to this cave and enjoy treats and triumphs, won’t you share them with me?”

Aydahn was savvy, Aydahn was quick, but when else in his life could he target the sun with a trick?

He stepped into the cave, with a smile on his lips. A sparkle in his eyes and a swagger on his hips. In the cavern he found nothing, but the flickering flame; a flash of claws later and he was never the same.

His fur turned black, like the soot of a fire. His eyes turned gold like a funeral pyre. When asked by the elders what he saw in the dark, he whispered of light, of embers and sparks. A crown like corona and horns wreathed in flame, the most beautiful thing he could ever claim.

The demon of embers, reached into his heart, took hold of his future and tore it apart.

So beware, my cubs, of lights in the night, and promises and secrets that burn far too bright.
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.3.Title: Dragonscorched Ledger
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.3.Text:
The beast that cast us from our homes is a fickle sort, laughing as he torches our settlements and watches us flee. He’s like a child, holding a crystal to ants and watching them burn. We are the ants, and now I find myself apologising to the anthills as I pass.

It would be enough to assume the dragon is reckless and cruel, yet there is something else I have noticed as I follow him across the dunes. In moments where he thinks no one is watching, he raises his claws to the heavens and sings to the sun.

If I were a different person, one with less anger in his heart, I could see faith in his actions; hope in his heart. As if he praises the sunlight, our villages some sacrificial offering to his god in the sky.

Could it be true? It makes a twisted sort of sense. This creature, this beast of flame and fury, could be setting fire to our villages, burning down our homes, as some dread act of worship for his nameless god.

It brings to mind legends of the demon of the suns. As my grandmother told them to me, the demon would appear to people and offer them everything they had ever wanted, only to change them into mindless creatures of worship. 

How does one look into a fire and see only the light, not the flame, or the ashes.
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.4.Title: Everburning Book
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.4.Text:
Our city is lost to embers, great monuments crumbling beneath the scorching heat of the sun and the claws of the dragon. We were peaceful, we were no threat to him, yet he brought such a fury down upon us that we could not stand against him.

Our archers fired so many arrows that it blotted out the sun. Our mages hurled spells that shook the very foundations of the earth, and our warriors readied their blades so sharp that they could cleave a mountain in two.

All for nought.

As he razed our cities, and shattered the monuments that recorded our past, he sang. Sang a song to the heavens, a great hymn to the sky. A song that burned in our hearts, igniting our souls like we were kindling on the fire just waiting for a spark.

We ran. What else could we do?

How do you fight a foe that threatens to set your spirit aflame?

We wander now, disparate tribes, keeping far enough away from each other, in the hope that he cannot chase us all. Families separated. A culture buried in the sands.

I only hope that we can find ourselves again, free from Fuzan’s flames.
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.5.Title: Sand-weathered Book
KeysToEntries.QoA.Book.5.Text:
Grandmother died today. She walked out into the desert, into the scorching sun and let the sands take her.

She was always smiling, was grandmother, always had a story to tell. She loved us dearly, even with her last breath. It’s a lesser mentioned part of the bargain with the dragon, this sacrifice at the end of our days. To burn in the sunlight. To vanish into the storm. We sacrifice our last moments, so that our loved ones get to enjoy far more of theirs. The Mark, this symbol of Fuzan's that we carry as protection against his wrath, it compels us to the wilderness. Makes us an offering to the storm. 

In doing so the rest of us are spared and benefit from Fuzan's mercy. He turns his flames away from us. Protects us against some of the dangers of the desert, in exchange for the Mark. Grandmother's last thoughts would have been of the rest of us. As was always her way. 

It still hurts, though, this grief. She could have had years, at least, her fur had barely greyed in her age. The village feels so silent now, without her cackling laughter.

But we live on. Her sacrifice guarantees that.

Perhaps, one day, I will walk out into those sands. I wonder if I will be as brave as grandmother was?
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.1.Title: Dusty Tome
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.1.Text:
I was visited once, by a strange creature who spoke as if witnessing a time that wasn’t now. I was lying in my bed, when they appeared out of the dunes and told me this tale as if I were someone else.

They referred to me as an adventurer, but I have never left my home. Still, it was a strange enough event that I felt I should record it.

It was on the subject of the lava-creatures that we see shambling around under Fuzan’s direction – the KotHaar. These creatures, they claimed, were here long before the dragon. Long before anyone set foot on Ashenfall, perhaps even Gielinor itself. When the ancient ones - the elder gods, as they called them – settled on this world, they brought with them servitors who watched over the secrets of this place, and the treasures within it.

They had no name at the time, and no need for one, for each was defined by their purpose. A taskworker with a soul.

My narrator explained that they were guarding some sort of device, a powerful tool that kept the sun shining and brightness that let the world thrive, rather than burn. A device, they claimed, has now been perverted by the dragon into some monstrous device that is destroying the region.

Adventurer, if you read this, as I suspect my narrator predicts, please find a way to relinquish the dragon’s hold on this device, this Lens, so that the world may not come to fear the light of day.
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.2.Title: Obsidian- carved Book
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.2.Text:
Words are a strange concept. Pointless. We should know our purpose. Know our place. There is no reason to share sounds with others.

Or there should not be. Yet the KotHaar  are changed. Where once we knew our purpose. Once we knew what needed to be done. Now the flames that move us twist away from us, forcing us to act in purpose other than what we have known.

The Lens is taken. KotHaar carried it from its resting place and brought it to the volcano where it is now twisted, also, against its purpose.

We must learn the language of the mortal races, so that the danger can be known. This One leaves this scripture so others may come to understand the danger. 

The Lens is misaligned. The sun burns too bright. The KotHaar are not ourselves.

We do not wish to do this.

Our purpose has been corrupted by the fire within us. The Cave of Screams strips us of choice, and lets the flame seize control. It moves us against our commands. We are puppets, and a monster has the strings.
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.3.Title: Soot-stained Ledger
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.3.Text:
I have followed these strange creatures across the sands. They are his agents, this much is true, but what is their purpose and how did the dragon come to acquire such tools?

I saw once, one of them, dragged up from the sands, pulled along by an invisible force in their chest, their arms and legs dangling strangely as if they were not in control of their actions. The dragon stood before them, claw clenched and a mad glean in his eyes as he chuckled to himself at his new toys.

Then? Then he made them fight. Took two of the creatures, gave them weapons and clapped his hands gleefully as they tore each other apart.

Yet, I felt no animosity from the creatures to one another. No anger bubbled in the air like it so often does. The entire scene played with the cold delivery of a lecture, even as the loser of the battle turned cold on the sand.

At this death, this act of violence, Fuzan roared with laughter into the sky. Then held his hands up to the light of the sun in some strange sort of reverence.

I wish I understood what I saw here. Perhaps I shall study them some more.
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.4.Title: Partially-melted Journal
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.4.Text:
Long ago, there were people beneath the sand. They dwelled in the caverns at the heart of the world, tending to ancient mysteries well beyond our understanding.

In my travels I once found a cave, barely visible in the sandstorms, and within that cave were ancient paintings of four armed beings, wreathed in flame.

I do not know who drew them. Indeed, from what I can gather there was no one in this land that could. Yet, there they were, as clear as the scorching sun above us.

These paintings showed the creatures in supplication before a great towering creature, something like a snake, or a worm, yet far more terrible. The worm, and its followers, were gathered around a crack on the wall in which strange lines of smoke had been drawn, as if they were fighting back the smoke somehow, pushing it back into the crack. 

I have no idea what it references, or what it means, but for some reason the image haunts me each night I sleep. I dream of smoke, crawling out of cracks in the world and attempting to strangle me. 

I never found the cave again. I have searched and searched, retracing my steps time and time again, yet there is no sign of it.

I wonder what other secrets have been buried by the sands?
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.5.Title: Sand-scoured Diary
KeysToEntries.KotHaar.Book.5.Text:
I found one of the rock people lying in the sand. He, if I should give them a gender, was only faintly glowing, as if the magma within him were cooling, turning into rock.

Should I have left him there? Perhaps. Certainly father would tell me so. They are the reason so many of my kinfolk are dead; their raids, against our caravans, are the reason so many starve in the fallow seasons. Yet, I found I could not just leave him alone in those last moments. No one should die in silence, without at least a chance to confess their fears.

His eyes - strange and shimmering, like they were carved from rock and placed upon his features – were somehow full of feeling, as if he were flesh and blood. He was afraid. Sad. Lost. I felt sorry for the creature, how strange is that?

The magma cooled around him, seeping out in some places as if he were wounded and bleeding out into the dunes. His limbs lay cold and useless by his sides, his entire existence locked in place at his torso as the cold spread slowly up his body, snuffing out his light.

A sound scratched from within him. The sound of it was like rocks scraping together. A hollow, cold thing, carrying with it a single word that I thought they didn’t even know.

“Sorry,” he said, as the last embers went dark.

I buried him in the sands, and left a marker for his kin to find. If they even look for their fallen. I’m not even sure they bury their dead.
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.1.Title: Dragonkin Journal
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.2.Text:
The kalphite are creatures of the desert, so they are at home here. It was trivial enough to steal a royal egg from their hive on the mainland, and bring it back here for study, and with each iteration of the brood I find myself more and more intrigued.

At first I thought they were a hive mind, the pinnacle of my research, but the more I learn, the more I realise that it’s not a singular consciousness, but a singular consensus. The queen demands and the hive obeys. They serve her because to serve her is right. The hive comes first and without the queen there is no hive.

This makes it annoyingly difficult to gather tissue samples from her, however. The soldiers, feeble as they are, gather around her like a protective wall and I must expend far more effort than is reasonable just to take a little blood, or a few of her eyes.

It’s fine, they grow back.
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.1.Text:
The Aughra creed have long been focused on escaping the curse by escaping our physical selves. They seek to project their consciousnesses into new forms, shapes and species. At first we considered the dragons, but they were still, in their own way, afflicted by the curse and so we cast our nets wider and wider seeking new forms to take.

Yet each of them is so limited in their ambitions. They seek a single form. A single mind. A single will locked into a singular vessel. While I would argue that we can be so much more.

Insects have long fascinated me. They are a collection of individual minds, small and unimpressive, true, but they work in such harmony that they act as a cohesive whole. Ants, bees and so forth, rally together creating micro-civilisations acting for a greater good. Imagine, for a moment, if you could turn that cooperative system to something bigger.

One mind, guiding a swarm. One soul as an endless wave of limbs, each pushing toward the same purpose. Why, with the right bodies, I could build a city in a day. I could put Braka’s loftiest ambitions to shame.

If I could just find the right swarm to become, I’m sure I could make even the Roakin tremble at my potential.
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.2.Title: Avisk’s Musings
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.3.Title: Entomologist’s Journal
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.3.Text:
The bugs fascinate me, even if my husband thinks I’m bonkers. He says “Niamh, I love you, but you can’t pin one of those things to the wall and call it art. At least wash it first, it stinks.”

Well! I mean, you absolutely can, though it takes quite a while and you need a particularly sturdy nail, but it CAN be done!

Anyway, where was I? So, I followed the bugs to their hive and, wow, just… just wow! They may be dumb, brainless crawly things, but they can make some wonderful structures. There’s an artistry to them that’s all the more impressive considering they have the aesthetic sensibilities of… well… insects.

Perhaps its their nature? They are so colourful after all. Their shells are so sparkly, and their wings reflect myriad colours in the noonday sun. Creatures as beautiful as these must be born with artist souls, surely?

I found some old notes in that horrible pyramid thing. Some madman talking about crystals and helixes and other such nonsense, but what I did find was that these bugs aren't from around here. They were stolen from another bug hive, really far away. On another continent, perhaps the one my people fled from thousands of years ago. I wonder if the bugs there are as fascinating as these, or did the journey change them somehow? Would two hives look identical to one another? Are their queens connected somehow? Can they talk to each other across continental differences? Would they get on with one another? Would they go to war? 

So many questions!

I need better notes. 

I think I’ll try and get a bit closer. I wonder what the hives look like on the inside? I’m sure they’ll welcome me in.
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.4.Title: Avisk’s Experiment Log
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.4.Text:
Experiment 17

I used some of the crystal on one of the insects. Took a little effort, but I stitched it into their skin as close to their nervous system as was possible.

Focusing my will upon the creature demonstrated limited results. A few controlled twitches here, a mandible click there, but nothing substantial. I  will need to consider more carefully.



Experiment 32

I embedded the crystals in the eggs this time. It occurred to me that the best way to bind the creature to the crystal was in this gestational period. The embryos grow around the shards and the energies infuse them from an early stage.

When I focus my will, I can control the movements of one of them for a limited time. I can almost see through their senses, not quite full transference, but the start of it. As they age, however, growing in size, they resist my efforts. So this is a short-lived solution at best. Still, interesting enough.



Experiment 42

The helix! This will be the answer, my means of subsuming the Kalphite consciousness beneath my will. A perfect blend of crystals, designed to resonate and redirect the mental energies of the hive, so that my will may replace them. It's like a series of mirrors, redirecting a single source of light to multiple places. Once installed, the helix shall turn my mind into the origin of all Kalphite consciousness! 

I just need the time to get it all in place. 



Experiment 59

The dragons have turned against us and I run out of time to perfect my experiments with the Kalphite hive. Yet, I believe I have a breakthrough that might lead to my apotheosis, the Dreaming Stone. With great effort, and alchemy, having stolen much of Lacrussa’s resources – well she won’t need them now she’s dead – I have created a crystal large enough to house my full consciousness. From there, I shall project my mind into the Kalphite queen and then connect her thoughts to her offspring via the crystals embedded in each of them.

It may not work, but I have little time for iteration. The dragons are at my door, and that red-scaled imbecile will soon find a way to feed me to his mother. Well, they can have the shell, but my mind, my genius, shall live forever!
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.5.Title: Bug Catcher’s Diary
KeysToEntries.Kalphite.Book.5.Text:
Today is the day I catch one of them bugs. I’m gonna lure it in with some vulture meat and then I’ll trap it with my net and force it to be my friend.

We will go on grand adventures, and maybe I’ll find other bug catchers, like me, and make our kalphites fight. Mine will win of course, she’s going to be the biggest and bestest, I’ll call her Chompy.

Dad says it’s silly to like bugs. He says a good cub should like hunting and fishing and I don’t know, climbing rocks? I stop listening after a bit. He’s all old and greying and doesn’t like adventure.

My new friend, who lives in the crystal, tells me that the bugs are awesome and tells me all about a great big hive where a really big bug lives. I’m going to go and find it and its going to be my friend.

Chompy and me will be bestest friends forever!
KeysToEntries.WolfandGoddess.Book.1.Text:
Dearg Due was loved and so was rewarded
Night would not fall on her mortal life.
But Dearg Due felt guilt for a gift undeserv-ed.

Cruel verse, cruel verse, the gift meets a curse.

Dearg Due bore her gift to a many-headed fiend.
She jumped into its maw – an immortal strike.
She tore and she rent, but fortune forsake her.

Cruel verse, cruel verse, the gift meets a curse.

The dragon cursed the wolf within its own gullet.
Dearg Due was doused in eternal unlife.
Spat back to Manafem, she stalked the sand, listless.

Cruel verse, cruel verse, the gift meets a curse
KeysToEntries.WolfandGoddess.Book.Title: The Wolf and the Goddess
